transcript.sourceText: THE CORE IDEA
transcript.text: THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: The Federal Reserve conducts monetary policy, supplies reserve balances, supports payments, and serves as lender of last resort. Its structure includes the Board of Governors and 12 regional Reserve Banks; the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) directs monetary policy. Operational independence allows policy decisions without day-to-day political approval within a mandate set by Congress. The Treasury manages federal finances rather than monetary policy.

runs.text: The Federal Reserve buys Treasury securities from a bank, adding reserve balances. In the limited-reserves textbook model, this tends to lower short-term rates; in an ample-reserves system, administered rates are the main rate-control tool. The purchase is monetary policy, not a change in federal taxes or spending.

THE CORE IDEA

The Federal Reserve conducts monetary policy, supplies reserve balances, supports payments, and serves as lender of last resort. Its structure includes the Board of Governors and 12 regional Reserve Banks; the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) directs monetary policy. Operational independence allows policy decisions without day-to-day political approval within a mandate set by Congress. The Treasury manages federal finances rather than monetary policy.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
The Federal Reserve conducts monetary policy; the Treasury manages federal finances.
The FOMC sets the monetary-policy stance and directs open-market operations.
Commercial banks issue deposits; the central bank issues the reserve balances banks use for payments.
WATCH OUT
